overview: White develops both knights and keeps the e4 pawn defended instead of fighting for the centre. Black can play 3...dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 (or Nd7 and Nf6) and reach a Caro-Kann Classical set-up with the Nf3 move already in, or 3...Bg4 with the Mindeno Variation. The game is a quiet, positional Caro-Kann in which Black equalises comfortably.

white_ideas.idea: Develop naturally with Nf3, Be2 or Bd3, and h3 to meet ...Bg4.
Keep options of d4 for a normal Caro-Kann centre.

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and develop the light bishop outside the chain.
Play ...Bg4 and ...e6 to pin the f3 knight.

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann Classical structure with d4 against c6-e6 and a half-open d-file.

character.notes: Quiet and safe for both. Solid.

gambit.notes: e4 pawn comes back by force.

structure.notes: Asymmetric Caro centre with a half-open d-file.

approach.notes: A normal alternative to 3.e5 and 3.exd5; standard.

plan_phrases: good light bishop outside the chain

sublines_that_differ.name: Mindeno Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Nf3 Bg4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black pins the knight and ...Bxf3 gives an unusual structure.

character.reason: Quiet Caro-Kann lines that are hard to break down.

structure.reason: Fixed asymmetric centre with a half-open d-file.

approach.reason: Played by strong players now and then.
